questions.question: 10 units must be bought. Supplier A charges a fee of 10 if used plus 3 per unit, for at most 6 units; supplier B charges a fee of 2 if used plus 4 per unit, for at most 10 units. A heuristic buys as much as possible from the lowest unit price first. What does its plan cost?

A tour must start at town A, visit B, C and D once each and return to A. Distances: AB 2, AC 3, AD 4, BC 6, BD 1, CD 5. The nearest-neighbour heuristic always moves to the closest unvisited town. What is the length of its tour?
For a cost-minimization problem, a heuristic finds a plan that satisfies every constraint and costs 52. A colleague's method, claimed to be exact, reports an optimal cost of 55. What follows?
options: 55 cannot be the optimal cost, since a feasible plan costing only 52 exists.
The heuristic plan must be infeasible, as heuristics cannot beat exact methods.
Both can be right, since heuristics and exact methods measure different costs.
The optimal cost is exactly 52, since the heuristic beat the exact method.

questions.question: Four towns have distances AB 1, AC 2, AD 5, BC 3, BD 4, CD 6. A tour starts and ends at A and visits each other town once. Nearest neighbour from A gives A, B, C, D, A with length 15. What does comparing it with the other tours show?
options: Tour A, B, D, C, A has length 13, so nearest neighbour is not optimal.
Nearest neighbour is optimal, since every move goes to the closest town.
Reversing the tour to A, D, C, B, A shortens it to 13 kilometres.
Every tour has length 15, since each town is visited exactly once.

questions.question: A knapsack holds at most 12 kg; items A (7 kg, value 10), B (6 kg, 8), C (6 kg, 8), D (5 kg, 4). Greedy-by-value packs A and D (value 14). No exchange of one packed item for one unpacked item gives a feasible packing of higher value. Is A and D optimal?
options: Yes; no single exchange improves it, so it is optimal.
Yes; greedy by value is optimal when weights are whole kilograms.
No; A, B and D are together worth 22.
No; B and C together weigh 12 kg and are worth 16.

questions.question: For maximize $x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\le8$, $3x_1+x_2\le9$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, a heuristic sets $x_2=0$ and makes $x_1$ as large as possible, giving $(3,0)$ with value 3. A planner concludes that no feasible plan exceeds 3. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The claim holds, because the heuristic plan satisfies every constraint.
The claim holds unless the heuristic broke one of the two constraints.
Only $z^*\ge3$; the feasible point $(2,3)$ gives 5, so the claim fails.
$z^*\le3$, which a better heuristic could later raise above 3.
